chapter: Ellington colleagues, singers and world tours
title: Herb Jeffries and Flamingo
summary: Jeffries began with Jump for Joy, and his Flamingo record is hard to duplicate.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: It is -- right, how about Herb Jeffries?
Herb had a stint here at a club a few weeks ago. I never got to see him, but he appeared here at a night club, and I hear it was very nice, very much like the old Herb Jeffries, but --
He's singing pretty well,
(Unintelligible).
-- I never got to see him. So I don't know too much about him, where he lives and what --
And he was in the band a long time, wasn't he? How long was he --
Oh, years and years and years.
In the band?
He was out. He wasn't with the band.
But when -- he actually worked with Duke how long?
I imagine it was couple of years, two, three years. Could be wrong, because I'm not too accurate on dates.
Well, he worked in "Jump For Joy".
Oh, yes, that was his big beginning.
And was his first record with the band "Flamingo" (inaudible)?
No, I don't think it was. That was his
most noted record, I believe.
And Duke used to say that Billy Strayhorn changed vocal arranging around with his arrangement of 'Flamingo' for her for that record.
Yeah, okay.
(Laughter)
You would say something different (inaudible)?

No, I think he -- his voice just fit that particular tune. In fact, the record that he made on 'Flamingo' hasn't been duplicated since or hasn't been tried too much since. It was rumored that so many of them refused to try it because Herb had -- Herbie had done such a good job on it, and they didn't care to risk it. So --
